Case :- Application U/S 528 Bnss No. - 28045 of 2025
Applicant :- Sanjeev Mishra And 4 Others
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Dileep Kumar Shukla
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Vikas Budhwar,J.
1. Vakalatnama of Ravi Kumar Singh (AoR No.A/R 1166/12) filed today on behalf of O.P. No.2 is
taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Dileep Kumar Shukla, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Bhuwal Vishwakarma,
learned A.G.A. for the State and Sri Ravi Kumar Singh, learned counsel for O.P. No. 2.
3.

This application has been preferred for quashing of the proceedings of Complaint Case No.78/2022, (Kajal Sharma vs. Sanjeev Mishra & others), under Sections 498A, 323, 494 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station -Mahila Thana Bahjoi, District Sambhal,
pending in the Court of Civil Judge (Junior Division)/F.T.C., Sambhal at Chandausi and also to quash the summoning order dated 05.08.2022 passed by the learned Civil Judge (Junior Division)/Fast Track Court, Sambhal at Chandausi in the aforesaid complaint case.

The applicant herein had earlier approached this Court while filing Application u/s 482 CrPC No.41794 of 2024, Sanjeev Mishra and others vs. State of U.P. and another, in which on 05.12.2024,
following order was passed:-
"1. Vakalatnama, filed by Sri Ravi Kumar Singh, learned counsel appearing for opposite party No.2, is taken on record.
2. Heard Sri Dileep Kr. Shukla, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Ravi Kr. Singh,
learned counsel for opposite party No.2 and Sri Raj Bahadur Verma, learned A.G.A.
for the State.
3.

sentences.text:
The instant application has been filed seeking quashing of the entire proceeding of Complaint Case No. 78 of 2022 (Kajal Sharma vs. Sanjeev Mishra and others), under Section 498-A, 323, 494 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S. Mahila Thana Bahjoi,
District Sambhal, pending before Civil Judge (J.D.)/ F.T.C., Sambhal at Chandausi.

entities.text: Kajal Sharma vs. Sanjeev Mishra and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. It is jointly contended by learned counsel for the applicants as well as opposite party No.2 that the parties have settled their dispute amicably and a written compromise dated 2.9.2024 has also been entered into between the parties.
It is further submitted that a copy of the compromise has been filed before the Civil Judge (J.D.)/J.M. Sambhal at Chandausi.
It is, therefore, requested that the impugned proceeding may be quashed.
5. Learned A.G.A. points out that the aforesaid compromise is yet to be verified by the court below, therefore, a direction may be issued for verification of the same.

6. Considering the fact that the parties have settled their dispute amicably and this fact is not disputed by opposite party No.2, the application is disposed of with a direction to the court below that it will verify the said compromise after summoning the parties within a period of two months from the date of receiving a copy of this order.
7.
For a period of two months, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants in the aforesaid case.

8. It is further provided that the parties are at liberty to file a fresh application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. to quash the impugned proceeding on the basis of verified compromise."
5.

Learned counsel for the applicants has invited attention towards Annexure-2 at page-17 and 19 of the paper-book so as to contend that the compromise stood verified on 20.12.204 by the Court of Civil Judge (J.D.)/ F.T.C., Sambhal at Chandausi.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Relevant averment has been made in para-7 of the application.

sentences.text: 6. Learned A.G.A. as well as counsel for O.P. No. 2 do not dispute the said fact.

7. Considering the submissions of the rival parties as well as stand taken by them, in view of the judgment in case of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303 and State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Laxmi Narayan, 2019 (5) SCC 688 this Court does not find any justification to further proceed.

sentences.text: 8. Accordingly, the application stands allowed.

9. The proceedings of Complaint Case No.78/2022, (Kajal Sharma vs. Sanjeev Mishra & others),
under Sections 498A, 323, 494 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station -Mahila Thana Bahjoi, District Sambhal, pending in the Court of Civil Judge (Junior Division)/F.T.C., Sambhal at Chandausi and also the summoning order dated 05.08.2022 passed by the learned Civil Judge (Junior Division)/Fast Track Court, Sambhal at Chandausi in the aforesaid complaint case stand quashed in respect to the applicants.
